plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $27, I should bid $27 to maximize expected profit, regardless of what others bid.

This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value (negative profit). If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $20.
